title: Идея отправить маму на балет  (The Idea to Send Mom to the Ballet)

segments.t: Learning that Chef Barinov's romantic evening in the office fell apart, Senya and Fedya joke about TV commercials before suggesting he invite Elena home while his mother is out at the ballet. Inspired, Barinov immediately hatches a plan to clear Lyova's apartment.
Ах ты, бог ты мой, не переживай.
Там в перерывах много чего советуют.
А можно я сегодня уйду пораньше?

'So how did it go?' Max brings out the contrast between 'come on' and 'what' in a few short words.
'It did not work out.' The meaning hinges on 'not' working together with 'worked out' in spoken Russian. Max answers right away.

'Oh, good grief, do not worry about it.' In Russian, the idea of 'oh' flows naturally into 'worry' without extra filler words.
'At the end of the day.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'end' before landing on 'ends'.
'You watch football on TV, right?' Max brings out the contrast between 'you' and 'on earth' in a few short words. Kostya answers right away.

'What about inviting her to your home?' The grammar packs 'and' and 'to invite' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Send your mother where?' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'where to' and 'to send' in a few short words.
'To the cinema or the ballet, there you go.' In Russian, the idea of 'the cinema' flows naturally into 'there you go' without extra filler words. Kostya answers right away.
'For the entire night?' In Russian, the idea of 'on' flows naturally into 'night' without extra filler words.

'Could I please leave a little early today?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'a bit earlier'. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.
